title: Tesla's mental electricity model
summary: Seven theses on Tesla's ether model, and how the old ether-vs-monad dispute was resolved by quantum field theory.

body.heading: One universal medium
paragraphs: One universal medium (ether) fills all space. Everything — matter, energy, forces — are states or motions of this single substance.

Electricity behaves like an incompressible fluid. It is a continuous quantity that cannot be created or destroyed, only moved. Charge is tension in the medium; current is the equalization flow of those strains; magnetism is the circular motion of the medium around conductors.

body.heading: Matter as whirls
paragraphs: Matter itself is just whirls and vortices of the medium. Hence Tesla's famous claim: there is no energy in matter other than that received from the environment — atoms are machines driven by the surrounding ether, which is why he rejected E=mc².

body.heading: Energy in the space around wires
paragraphs: Energy travels in the space around wires, not inside them. The conductor just guides; the real transfer happens through the dielectric via displacement currents. He pushed this to the extreme with high voltage and high frequency.

His waves were pressure pulses, not Hertz's transverse waves — sound-like longitudinal disturbances in the medium, propagating through Earth and air. The Earth is a resonant conductor; pump it at the right frequency and it rings like a bell, letting power be drawn anywhere — the premise of Wardenclyffe.
No electrons. Cathode rays weren't particle streams; radioactivity didn't mean atoms store nuclear energy; his cosmic rays outran light.

body.heading: The monad connection
paragraphs: His model is essentially monist metaphysics operationalized. Everything is whirls and strains of one medium; matter, electricity, light, and gravity are just different motions of the same substance. He inherited it from Faraday–Maxwell continuum physics plus the era's monist philosophy.

The modern irony: quantum field theory looks like a final marriage — continuous fields everywhere (ether-like, minus the mechanical medium) whose quanta are discrete units (monad-like). The three-hundred-year-old dispute got synthesized rather than won.
